subject: POC orchestration: scheduling hands-on + routing-tier workshop
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@auroraretail.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroraretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: POC orchestration: scheduling hands-on + routing-tier workshop

Hi Ethan / Maya —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, Aurora Retail is ready to move from the quick demo to a short POC: a kickoff + a hands-on working session where we'll run prompt review, routing policy design (model selection, region/tiering, fallback rules), and a short load test (targeting your steady-state 2–3k rps window).

Proposed slots (all PT):
- Wed Apr 28, 10:00–12:30 — kickoff + prompt review + model selection (2.5h)
- Thu Apr 29, 09:30–12:30 — hands-on routing workshop + load test (3h)

If those two half-days don’t work we can compress into a single full-day session — happy to be flexible. I attached a draft agenda and a sample traffic CSV so you can confirm the workload shape.

Quick asks from your side before we lock calendar:
- Confirm primary attendees and their roles (engineer, infra, product).
- Confirm which region(s) you want routing tested in (us-west/us-east/eu).
- Any data-handling constraints for the load test (PII, anonymization).

I'll loop in Lauren for any security/compliance questions and Monica to coordinate the load generator.

Thanks — look forward to getting this scheduled.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime
Attachments: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf (application/pdf), sample-traffic-10k-requests.csv (text/csv)

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@auroraretail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroraretail.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC orchestration: scheduling hands-on + routing-tier workshop

Thanks Priyom — this looks great. Quick notes:
- Wed Apr 28 conflicts with an all-hands for our ops team. Thu Apr 29 morning would work for us, but our infra lead (Ethan Parker) is traveling after 12:00 PT.
- Could we do Thu Apr 29 09:30–13:30 PT to give us 4 hours (split: 1h kickoff + 3h workshop/load)? That gives a buffer for extra testing.
- We'd like the load test to exercise both us-west and eu-west routing to validate geo-fallback behavior.

Attendees I'll confirm, but tentatively: Ethan Cole (product), Maya Singh (eng), Ethan Parker (infra, partial), Priya Rao (security — TBD).

Also: can you surface recommended model variants and the fallback policy you'd propose for retail queries that hit cold contexts? We'd like a short pre-read if possible.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Cole | Head of Product, Aurora Retail

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@auroraretail.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroraretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC orchestration: scheduling hands-on + routing-tier workshop

Ethan — Thu Apr 29 09:30–13:30 PT works for us. I'll hold that window provisional and send a formal invite once you confirm attendees.

On your asks:
- Pre-read: attaching a short note that outlines candidate model variants (gpt-retail-1-small / gpt-retail-1-medium / gpt-robust-quant), recommended quantization/latency tradeoffs, and a sample fallback flow (e.g., medium -> small -> cached response). Please treat the doc as a starting point — we'll make choices together during the kickoff.
- Regions: we'll prepare test endpoints in us-west and eu-west; Monica will coordinate the load generator to direct percent traffic to each region.
- Data constraints: noted — if any PII exists in the sample traffic please send a redacted file; otherwise we'll run anonymized synthetic variations.

Action items before invite:
1) Ethan / Maya: confirm final attendee list and any guest Zoom/SAML constraints.
2) Aurora: confirm whether you want us to run a cold-cache vs warm-cache scenario (we recommend both, short warm-up).
3) Redwood: Monica to share the load generator plan + resource estimate.

Attaching: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf, sample-traffic-10k-requests.csv.

I'll draft a meeting invite with two agenda blocks (kickoff: objectives + pre-read discussion; workshop: live routing config, tiering decisions, and a 30–45m load ramp).

— Priyom
Attachments: POC-Agenda-v1.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-model-variants-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Load plan and ownership for Aurora POC (draft)

Internal note — copying here so the invite reflects accurate run-of-show.

Planned test matrix (draft):
- Warm-cache baseline: 5 min steady @ 1k rps per region (us-west, eu-west)
- Cold-cache ramp: start 0 -> target 2k rps over 15 minutes (observe token latency and KV cache hit behavior)
- Fallback validation: inject intermittent model unavailability in us-west and measure automatic region routing to eu-west and model-tier fallback (medium -> small)

Owners:
- Load generator config & infra: Monica Patel (primary), Aditya Rao (support)
- Model selection & kernel paths: Priyom Das (lead), Lauren Bishop (security checks)
- Customer coordination & agenda: Priyom (lead), Monica (ops)

I'll prepare a one-page runbook we can attach to the invite (scripts, expected metrics, rollback triggers). Estimated infra cost: small (covered under POC credits), but will flag if we need additional reserved capacity.

— Monica

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@auroraretail.com>
